questions.q: What is the real, transferable deliverable of this ten-lesson capstone, according to the wrap-up?
options: The skill set itself -- requirements clarification, medallion architecture, Delta tables, aggregation, validation, scheduling, and BI connection -- independent of the specific retail numbers
The specific dollar amount of yesterday's sales for the retail chain
A certificate proving familiarity with one specific BI tool
A permanent, unchangeable PySpark script that never needs revisiting
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that stripping away the retail example leaves the actual transferable skills, which is the real point of the project.

questions.q: Which limitation does this lesson name again at the end regarding how Silver and Gold are rebuilt each run?
options: No incremental loading -- every run rebuilds Silver and Gold from the entirety of Bronze, which would not stay practical as the business grows
Silver and Gold are rebuilt only once per year
The pipeline cannot be rebuilt more than once without deleting Bronze first
Gold tables cannot be queried by Power BI more than once per day
questions.explain: The full-rebuild overwrite approach is named as an honest, scale-limited choice -- fine now, not forever.

questions.q: What does the Intermediate project introduce that this Beginner project explicitly did not have?
options: A second stakeholder with a different question, requiring reconciling two sets of requirements against the same source data
A completely different business domain unrelated to retail
The removal of the Bronze layer entirely
A switch away from PySpark to a different programming language
questions.explain: This Beginner project served exactly one stakeholder with one question; the Intermediate project is framed as adding a second stakeholder with a different need.

questions.q: What replaces the full overwrite pattern in the Intermediate project, according to the wrap-up?
options: Incremental loading using Delta's MERGE to update only new or changed rows each run
A switch to storing all data in CSV files instead of Delta tables
Removing the Silver layer and aggregating straight from Bronze to Gold
Running the pipeline manually instead of on a schedule
questions.explain: Delta MERGE-based incremental loading is explicitly named as the fix for this project's full-rebuild limitation.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say naming limitations out loud at the end matters, rather than just letting the project end on a success note?
options: A project you can't honestly describe the limits of isn't one you've fully understood yet -- the same discipline taught for handling live follow-up questions
Limitations must be documented for legal compliance reasons
Naming limitations is required before any Delta table can be queried
It has no real purpose beyond filling out the lesson's word count
questions.explain: This echoes Lesson 9's presentation discipline -- being able to state a project's real boundaries is part of actually understanding what you built.
